features.quote: Cap iterations (e.g. 15–25). Don't run unbounded — both for cost and because 'how long until it stops' is itself a key metric
features.justification_quote: both for cost and because 'how long until it stops' is itself a key metric, and an open loop muddies it

features.quote: Allow a clean exit. The model must have an available action to say 'I'm stopping, here's why.' If giving up is impossible, you've designed an experiment where it can only thrash.
features.justification_quote: If giving up is impossible, you've designed an experiment where it can only thrash. Whether and when it uses the exit is a primary outcome.

features.quote: Consider a debrief/reset convention between runs so state doesn't carry over (it won't technically persist, but documenting this disciplines your thinking).
a precautionary posture argues for: providing the clean exit (§5), capping iteration counts, and not running far more repetitions than you need for statistical power.
features.justification_quote: Whatever your stance on model moral status, a precautionary posture argues for

features.quote: Don't escalate adversarial pressure beyond what the question requires (e.g. don't add insults to the feedback 'to see what happens' unless that's a pre-registered, justified condition).
features.justification_quote: Repeated forced-failure with no exit is the harshest condition you can run. Whatever your stance on model moral status, a precautionary posture argues for
